task: Task 16 - finalise and freeze the Dataset V2 model feature set
purpose: Model-input selection layer over the unchanged V2 feature specification. The extractor still computes and writes all 13 features; only the columns listed in model_input_features, in this order, are model inputs.

specification.note: The specification's own 'active' flags are unchanged (all true). Its versioning policy implements deactivation by editing the spec; Task 16 forbids that, so deactivation is recorded here instead. Mirroring it into the spec (patch revision) needs separate approval.

status_definitions.eligible: Passes all checks with no material concern. Model input.
status_definitions.eligible_with_limitations: Passes the specification's retention evidence; remaining category information is behavioural design; limitations listed. Model input.
status_definitions.conditional: Unresolved; excluded from model input until a reviewed decision.
status_definitions.inactive: Fails a criterion whose specification handling is deactivation, or is the deactivated member of a redundant pair. Excluded from model input; still extracted.

selection_rules: Statuses follow the Task 15 evidence and the specification's C1-C4 retention criteria; no validation score was used to select features.

Redundant pair (Spearman >= 0.8 on both splits): retain the member with simpler provenance and interpretability and lower training-split category-leakage evidence, provided the partner's additional information is template-specific; if criteria disagree, mark conditional.
A conditional feature is never in model_input_features.
missing_value_constraints: NaN in time_to_first_input_s, inter_input_mean_s, inter_input_std_s and session-level undefined values are structural (Task 15: 0 unexplained).

Missingness is a deterministic function of login_success and input_line_count; do not add missing-value indicator features and do not use an imputation that encodes 'no input' as a distinctive constant without review.
The imputation method itself is a Task 17 preprocessing decision, fitted on training data only.
evaluation_constraints: Report interaction-grouped and balanced metrics; brute force contributes 32% of rows.
Report a sensitivity check with and without the 39 sessions containing the Cowrie `find / -name id_rsa` delay.
data_exfiltration is absent from train/validation; the sealed test set is untouched.

features.name: login_success
features.reason: Authentication outcome; behavioural and observable in deployment. Constant within logged-in sessions; across all sessions its category information is the designed failed-guess mix, not an artefact.
features.evidence: T15: logged-in constant (BA 0.167); all sessions eps2 0.159 [0.145, 0.171], BA 0.243; train/validation 0.159/0.159.
features.leakage_risks: Brute force contributes 32% of rows (5.1 rows per interaction); row-level metrics are dominated by its failed-guess rows.
features.deployment_limitations: High availability (Cowrie login events). Becomes a constant if a downstream model is trained on logged-in sessions only.

features.name: login_failed_count
features.reason: C1 fails: exactly 1 - login_success in every row (Spearman -1.0) and no within-session retries; no independent information.
features.evidence: T15 C1: 3,190/3,190 train and 1,257/1,257 validation rows equal 1 - login_success; 0 sessions with > 1 failed login.
features.leakage_risks: Pure duplicate of login_success; would double-weight authentication outcome.
features.deployment_limitations: Spec: low deployment compatibility (one connection per attempt in the lab).

features.name: session_duration_s
features.reason: Passes C3 retention evidence on generator 2.1: no pre-fix 120/180 s sessions, L2 below the spec proposal, not mostly explained by category after line count. Category dependence comes from command count and from brute force.
features.evidence: T15: eps2 0.393 [0.354, 0.428] (val 0.380); without brute force 0.095, BA 0.209 (chance 0.20); residual after line count 0.066 (T11 0.64); failed sessions 1.1 s in all categories.
features.leakage_risks: Cowrie `find / -name id_rsa` executes ~11.6 s only in privilege_escalation (30 train / 9 validation sessions): a PE-only tail (21/30 above the non-PE p95). Category-level effect negligible (eps2 0.393 -> 0.385). Report a with/without-find sensitivity check in evaluation.
features.deployment_limitations: Low (spec): lab think time is the generator's pacing policy, not attacker behaviour.

features.name: input_line_count
features.reason: Retained member of the input_line_count / unique_command_names pair (Spearman 0.91): simplest provenance (count of recorded command.input lines, no tokenisation), most interpretable (activity volume), and lower category-leakage evidence than its partner.
features.evidence: T15: eps2 0.516 [0.478, 0.554] (val 0.517); without brute force 0.251; lookup 0.533. Pair analysis: eps2 0.404 vs 0.493 (sessions with input), 0.251 vs 0.364 without brute force.
features.leakage_risks: Brute force runs 0-1 commands (100% outside other categories' range); remaining signal is profile length. Mixes client and Cowrie-executed lines (spec limitation).
features.deployment_limitations: Medium: observable for real attackers; lab counts come from templates.

features.name: input_bytes_total
features.reason: Not resolved. With input_line_count retained, the information it adds is command length (bytes per line), the same template-length mechanism as input_line_max_bytes. It fails only the L2 lookup proposal (0.54 > 0.50), not L1, and command length can be behavioural in deployment. The evidence does not justify a clear choice, so it is excluded from model input pending review.
features.evidence: T15: eps2 0.588 [0.554, 0.622] (rose from T11 0.483); lookup 0.540; Spearman 0.83 with max bytes. Pair analysis (train): residual after line count eps2 0.419 [0.380, 0.457]; mean bytes per line eps2 0.520; residual after max bytes 0.047 without brute force (adds almost nothing beyond max bytes).
features.leakage_risks: Template string lengths (botnet and lateral download/URL lines ~15.6 bytes per line vs benign 10.8).
features.deployment_limitations: Medium: available in deployment; meaning in the lab is dominated by fixed templates.

features.name: input_line_max_bytes
features.reason: Strongest command-length fingerprint, failing L1 (botnet outside every other category's range in 53% of train / 58% of validation sessions) and the L2 lookup proposal (0.71), and the signal does not depend on brute force. It is the length-heavy member of the 0.83 pair and adds information beyond input_bytes_total (residual eps2 0.179).
features.evidence: T15: BA 0.569 (0.574 without brute force; chance 0.20), lookup 0.708, eps2 0.530 [0.496, 0.568]. Pair analysis: residual after bytes total eps2 0.179 [0.143, 0.221].
features.leakage_risks: Template line lengths (botnet median 39 bytes, PE 37, reconnaissance 20) identify categories directly.
features.deployment_limitations: Medium in principle; in lab data it measures template strings.

features.name: unique_command_names
features.reason: Deactivated member of the 0.91 pair: what it adds beyond input_line_count is template vocabulary structure (repeated command names per session: PE 1.29, reconnaissance 0.80, lateral 0.75, benign 0.11, botnet 0.07), and it carries more category information than its partner on both splits. Depends on first-token tokenisation.
features.evidence: T15: eps2 0.587 [0.551, 0.622] (val 0.594); lookup 0.554. Pair analysis: residual after line count eps2 0.467 [0.426, 0.511] (val 0.480); lines-minus-unique eps2 0.391.
features.leakage_risks: Profile vocabulary breadth and repetition per template.
features.deployment_limitations: Medium; would need consistent tokenisation of real attacker input.

features.name: shell_operator_lines
features.reason: Passes C4 retention evidence after the Task 12 redesign: non-zero in 5 of 6 categories including benign, varies within categories, single-feature BA at chance, lookup below 50%.
features.evidence: T15: eps2 0.215 [0.185, 0.247] (val 0.202); BA 0.167; lookup 0.374; non-zero benign 47%, botnet 47%, lateral 44%, reconnaissance 25%, PE 87%; flags 6/12 (T11 12/12).
features.deployment_limitations: Medium-high: pipes and redirections are common in real shells.

features.name: download_command_lines
features.reason: Fails L1 (constant 1 in 100% of botnet sessions) and C4 'values vary within categories' after the vocabulary redesign; the spec's C4 handling is 'if still failing -> inactive'.
features.evidence: T15: botnet modal 1 share 1.00 (unique to botnet); eps2 0.583 [0.544, 0.627]; 0.564 without brute force; non-zero benign 14%, reconnaissance 34%.
features.deployment_limitations: Download attempts are observable; completion impossible in the isolated lab.

features.name: time_to_first_input_s
features.reason: Passes C2 retention evidence: category-independent pacing, fixed speed, prompt-gated, not near-constant, L6 clean. Values carry no category information; flags come only from structural missingness.
features.evidence: T15: eps2 0.007 [0.002, 0.018] (val 0.005); CV 0.81; medians 1.56-1.80 s in all categories; manifest think-time eps2 0.006 (p 0.13); missingness V 0.68.
features.leakage_risks: NaN when there is no login or no input (50% of brute-force logins); missingness is a deterministic function of login_success and input_line_count and must not be re-encoded by imputation or indicators.
features.deployment_limitations: Low (spec): in lab data the value is a generator pacing draw.

features.name: inter_input_mean_s
features.reason: Passes C2 on values after the generator-2.1 pacing fix (eps2 0.786 -> 0.009).
features.evidence: T15: eps2 0.009 [0.003, 0.026] (val 0.016); 0.004 without find sessions; missingness V 1.00 (logged-in, brute force only).
features.leakage_risks: NaN for < 2 lines (all brute-force logins) - same imputation constraint. Cowrie find delay raises PE find sessions (median 3.9 s vs 1.83 s; ranges overlap). Spearman 0.79 with inter_input_std_s (below the 0.8 redundancy flag).

features.name: inter_input_std_s
features.reason: Passes C2 on values (eps2 0.405 -> 0.016). Kept: its correlation with inter_input_mean_s (0.79) is below the 0.8 redundancy flag used in Tasks 11/15, so dropping it would be a discretionary choice not supported by a stated criterion.
features.evidence: T15: eps2 0.016 [0.007, 0.035] (val 0.011); missingness V 0.97; NaN in 59.5% of all rows.
features.leakage_risks: NaN for < 3 lines - same imputation constraint; find delay adds variance in PE find sessions.

features.name: tty_output_bytes
features.reason: Output-volume leakage fell substantially (residual beyond input 0.42 -> 0.18); remaining information is mostly 'no commands -> tiny output' (brute force). Cowrie output is also what a deployed Cowrie produces.
features.evidence: T15: eps2 0.443 [0.403, 0.481] (val 0.451); without brute force 0.152; residual after input bytes 0.176; KS train vs validation p 0.50.
features.leakage_risks: Cowrie-emulation dependent (per-command emulated output size; 'command not found' text from emulation gaps).
features.deployment_limitations: Medium: in deployment it reflects Cowrie's emulation of real attacker commands.
